Name: NATIONAL STUDENT CLEARINGHOUSE
OptOutMethod: NSC collects student data from education providers (institutions & industry credential providers (ICPs)) and discloses such data as contractually authorized in compliance with FERPA. FERPA allows disclosure of directory information (DI) without consent unless the student has opted-out, and NSC respects such opt-outs under FERPA. Individuals may opt-out of DI disclosures through their institution. Some ICPs may allow opt outs to collection or disclosure by NSC, which NSC also respects.
OptOutActivities: Pursuant to the requirements of FERPA, the directory information opt-out applies to disclosures where the individual has not consented to the disclosure and where no other exception to FERPA’s consent requirement applies. Industry credential opt outs would apply to collection by NSC or to NSC re-disclosures to education providers, agencies and organizations.
NonOptOutDataCollectionStatement: Under FERPA, the directory information opt-out does not apply to disclosures in which the individual has provided consent, or where an exception to FERPA’s consent requirement applies other than the directory information exception. Industry credential opt-outs would not apply to NSC’s re-disclosure, for the purpose of producing aggregate research, to entities agreed upon with the credential provider.
PurchaserCredentialingProcess: NSC ensures that the data we disclose as an agent of education providers goes to the proper parties, and is kept secure, through a thorough contracting process and a robust information security program. Data transfers are governed by a written contract which includes restrictions on the recipient’s use of the data, and all data is encrypted while in transit and at rest using the FIPS 140-2 guideline.  NSC has a credentialing process for entities that utilize our verification services.
ProvideStatementOnMinorsDataPractices: There are cases in which NSC has actual knowledge that it possesses such information on minors who are or who have been enrolled in higher educational institutions or earned an industry credential. We collect, maintain, and protect this data with the same robust policies we apply to all student data, and respect the same opt-outs as we do for non-minors. See our privacy policy at: https://www.studentclearinghouse.org/privacy-policy/.
AdditionalInfoOnDataPractices: NSC is a 31-year old non-profit, established in part by the higher education community, with a mission to serve the education and workforce communities and all learners with access to trusted data, related services, and insights. We only use student data as contractually authorized by our participating educational institutions and industry credential providers. For more about data privacy, see https://studentclearinghouse.org/about/our-privacy-commitment/.

OptOutActivities:
Consistent with the Acres' Privacy Policy, opt-outs apply to specific marketing, tracking, and data-sharing activities:

-Marketing Communications: You can opt out of direct marketing via email and text messages, including notifications for special promotions, offers, and events.
-Precise Geolocation: You can opt out of the collection of GPS coordinates and movement paths by disabling location services on your mobile device.
-Service-Related Communications: You cannot opt out of service-related or non-marketing emails, such as security alerts or administrative messages.
ThirdPartyOptOutAuthorization:

-General Requests: For standard Personal Information requests, the authorized agent must confirm their identity and authority in accordance with applicable law.
-Identity Verification: We may still ask the consumer for specific information to help confirm their identity directly.
NonOptOutDataCollectionStatement:

Legal and Safety Compliance: Personal Information may be used and disclosed without an opt-out when necessary to comply with applicable laws, respond to subpoenas, or cooperate with government authorities.
PurchaserCredentialingProcess:
Yes. There are inherent credentialing processes that exist for our Enterprise, Pro, and Plus customer tiers. Contracts with our data vendors include obligations for both parties to comply with all applicable data privacy protection laws, rules and regulations and contain restrictions on permitted use.  For Enterprise, there's a multi-stage vetting process that happens as a deal moves from initial discovery to a signed contract, Early in the cycle, Acres performs "Inbound Credentialing" to ensure the person we are talking to has the authority to buy (via BANT/MEDDIC and "Champion" checks) as well as the purpose for which the Enterprise Customer will be using the Acres services. Throughout the technical phase, we perform proofs of concept to ensure tech stacks are compatible and secure and our workflow meets the customer’s goals. Finally, during the contracting process, legal teams will redline any negotiable terms to ensure our privacy obligations are contractually honored and then we will move toward the contract execution / payment phase. 

When moving from Enterprise to self-serve (Pro and Plus) tiers, the credentialing process doesn't disappear; it just becomes automated, friction-less, and real-time. The goal is to lower the "barrier to entry" while still protecting the services and consumers from fraud, abuse, and legal liability. Self-serve customers must review our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service before creating an account, creating a paper trail for audit purposes. Our Terms of Service prohibit a customer from reselling any data they obtain through their Acres subscription. Since there is no salesperson involved at this stage, our system will verify the user is real by running a "bot" filter. Finally, when a user checks out on our site, our system uses Cloudflare to verify legitimate users and prevent automated abuse.  Additionally, our payment card processors conduct fraud scoring and detection on users of payment cards.
